why: Inserting the narrow_rule forced the model to avoid cuts immediately after clause- or phrase-introducing function words, so many cuts were shifted later (binding the following NP/clause into the preceding piece). That shift slightly improved alignment for moderate-depth budgets (bins ≤5–≤7) where multiple candidates are kept, but degraded the top-1 choice and the very short bin (≤3) because the strongest single cut was displaced or produced awkward fragmentation in quotes/NPs (illustrated by the worst examples where cuts moved off sentence-introductory markers onto nearby nouns/quotes).
lesson: A later revision should keep the binding of function words to following material limited so it benefits mid-depth rankings (≤5–≤7) without displacing top‑rank cuts or hurting the very short-piece bin (≤3).
